summary.prose: A sized bugfix ISSUE now routes into design.story carrying its own hash and story id, so the LLD is LLD-<issueHash>-s1 under the ISSUE's folder instead of a new standalone root. One shared definition of the one-implied-story rule is used by the chain report and the tracker resolver, so `insrc workflow chain` reports the ISSUE-anchored item's single story, and the chain report no longer says to run define. design.epic and the tracker keep refusing an ISSUE as an Epic; when they meet one they say so instead of advising a Define. Relationship change: LLD, PLAN, BUILD and review records of a bugfix share the ISSUE's epicHash (ISSUE 1 : 1 Story s1, the Story keyed by the same hash, no new stored field); existing LLDs and ISSUEs are unchanged. The tracker push, sync and post stages are out of scope: an ISSUE-anchored item skips them in the chain report, and ISSUE-5f9d4ab4c90c0b4c tracks making them handle an ISSUE. The JetBrains Workflows page reads artifact files directly and lists only DEF-anchored Epics; it now also lists an ISSUE-anchored item (one implied story s1, no HLD, no tracker step) so the IDE shows the same single story and next step as the chain report.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: Standalone feature — no parent HLD. Design directly against the repo, grounded on the s1 analyze passes. There are no HLD shared contracts to honour.

parameters.name: issue

parameters.name: repo

errors.condition: Magnitude is neither small nor sized (unchanged).
Sized route with a missing or non-hex issue.meta.issueHash; refused rather than letting design.story mint a new root.

preconditions: issue.meta.issueHash is the 16-hex hash of the stored ISSUE root

Existing fixtures that build an ISSUE for the sized route (the issue() builder in src/workflow/__tests__/bugfix-orchestration.test.ts and any advance fixture) carry a 16-hex meta.issueHash; every stored ISSUE already does.

The small route output is byte-for-byte unchanged

api.name: impliedIssueStories
api.signature: impliedIssueStories(issue: { readonly body: { readonly title: string } }): readonly { readonly id: string; readonly title: string }[]

parameters.name: issue
parameters.purpose: The ISSUE head whose story set is wanted.

returns.meaning: Exactly one entry: id 's1' (the single exported constant IMPLIED_ISSUE_STORY_ID) titled with the ISSUE title. The one place that states the one-implied-story rule; new, added next to readEpicDefinitionCore in src/workflow/storage.ts.

api.name: buildChainReport

parameters.name: epicHash
parameters.purpose: Work item hash; a DEF hash or an ISSUE hash.

returns.meaning: For a DEF-anchored item: unchanged. For an ISSUE-anchored item (no DEF, ISSUE root present; an ISSUE is equivalent to a define): the definition head is read as a discriminated value ({kind:'def', artifact: DefineArtifact} or {kind:'issue', artifact: IssueArtifact}); stories holds the implied s1 (from impliedIssueStories) with LLD existence and approval; each story path is built from the LLD's own meta (workItemAnchorCreatedAt, workItemKindOf, meta.epicSlug), as requireApprovedLld does, so it points under docs/standalone and not docs/epics; define reflects the ISSUE's existence, approval and rejection, with its path the ISSUE document; hld is absent and no HLD, amendment or staleness step applies. nextAction: ISSUE not approved -> approve-define whose command names the ISSUE document; ISSUE rejected -> run-define whose command reruns the issue stage (not define); then run-lld and approve-lld for s1; once s1's LLD is approved -> chain-complete. The tracker steps (push-tracker, sync-tracker) are skipped for an ISSUE-anchored item and left to ISSUE-5f9d4ab4c90c0b4c. When both a DEF and an ISSUE exist at one hash the DEF is read, as readEpicDefinitionCore does (design review separately refuses that state).

postconditions: No existing field is removed or retyped; one optional field is added so a client can tell the definition is an ISSUE
An ISSUE-anchored report never contains run-hld, approve-hld, review-amendment, refresh-stale, push-tracker or sync-tracker

api.name: readDefineArtifact

parameters.name: epicHash
parameters.purpose: Hash expected to name a DEF.

returns.meaning: Unchanged: still DEF-only, so requireApprovedEpic and every Epic-only caller keep refusing an ISSUE.

errors.condition: No DEF at that hash. When an ISSUE root exists at that hash the message names the work item as ISSUE-anchored (a bugfix has no Define or HLD) and does not tell the user to run define; otherwise the existing message is kept.

postconditions: The error class and the throwing condition are unchanged; only the message differs for an ISSUE-anchored hash

api.name: WorkflowChainReader.readAll

returns.meaning: One entry per DEF-*.json (unchanged) plus one entry per ISSUE-*.json whose hash has no DEF-*.json in the same artifacts directory (a hash with both lists once, as the DEF). An ISSUE entry has definitionKind 'issue'; define is the ISSUE's existence, approval (meta.approvedAt) and rejection (meta.rejectedAt); hld is absent; stories holds the one implied story s1 titled with the ISSUE body title, with hasLld and approved read from LLD-<hash>-s1.json and never stale; amendments are zero. nextActionHint for an ISSUE entry is a plain string: 'Approve issue' when unapproved, 'Re-run issue' when rejected, 'Design story s1' with no LLD, 'Approve LLD for s1' with an unapproved LLD, 'Chain complete' once approved; it never names an HLD, amendment or stale step. The tracker half stays out of the plugin as before. Existing DEF entries are unchanged.

preconditions: The reader stays read-only, opens no socket and never throws; a malformed ISSUE file contributes nothing, as a malformed DEF does
postconditions: WorkflowChainDto gains one field with a default, definitionKind: String = "def", so existing constructor callers and DEF entries are unchanged

dataModelChanges.details: params gains epicHash (string, the issue hash) and storyId (string, 's1'). Consumed by the daemon start phase, where an existing epicHash is preserved and storyId is already honoured (augmentStandaloneParams).

One optional field, definitionKind ('def' | 'issue'), records which artifact is the work item's definition; no field removed or retyped, so IDE clients that parse the report keep working. Internally the chain reads the definition through a discriminated DEF-or-ISSUE value instead of a bare DefineArtifact.

dataModelChanges.entity: Work item identity (ISSUE hash shared by LLD, PLAN, BUILD, review and chain records)
dataModelChanges.details: For a sized bugfix the LLD id is LLD-<issueHash>-s1, so every downstream record keys on the ISSUE's hash. standalone:true remains a folder and workflow layout flag (docs/standalone) and does not mean independent of the ISSUE. Folder label and anchor are inherited from the ISSUE by the existing finalizeStandaloneLld path; design review classifies the LLD as kind issue because the ISSUE root exists at that hash. No ISSUE or LLD record shape changes.

One field with a default, definitionKind ('def' | 'issue'), so the Workflows page and its tests that build the DTO by name keep compiling and DEF entries keep their value. The reader additionally enumerates ISSUE-*.json for hashes that have no DEF.

migration.stateBefore: The sized bugfix route emits design.story params without epicHash or storyId (src/workflow/bugfix/next-after-issue.ts:78), so the daemon start phase mints a new epicHash (src/daemon/steps/workflow-step/phases/start.ts:147) and the LLD is a new standalone root; design review then fails with 'Missing Epic/ISSUE provenance'. The chain report reads only a DEF (src/workflow/chain.ts:150, :161) and reports zero stories and run-define for an ISSUE-anchored item. readDefineArtifact (src/workflow/gates.ts:159) tells the user to run define. The one-implied-story rule exists only in src/workflow/tracker/resolve.ts:292.
migration.stateAfter: The sized route carries epicHash = the issue hash and storyId s1, so the LLD is LLD-<issueHash>-s1 in the ISSUE's folder. One shared constant and helper state the implied-story rule, used by the chain report and the tracker resolver. The chain report returns the implied s1 for an ISSUE-anchored item and never advises run-define for it; readDefineArtifact names the ISSUE-anchored situation. DEF-anchored items, genuine standalone features and Epic stories behave exactly as before.

migrationSteps.action: Add the shared implied-story constant and helper next to readEpicDefinitionCore and point tracker/resolve.ts storyEvidence at it; behaviour identical, covered by existing resolver tests.

Teach the chain report to read the work item's definition head as DEF or ISSUE and to build the implied story and next action from an ISSUE head; add one optional field on ChainReport naming the definition kind.
Change the ArtifactMissingError message of readDefineArtifact when an ISSUE root exists at the hash; error class and throw condition unchanged.
Add epicHash and storyId to the sized route of nextAfterIssue, with the invalid-issue-hash refusal; small route untouched.

Teach the JetBrains WorkflowChainReader to enumerate ISSUE-<hash>.json for hashes with no DEF and project them with the implied story s1 and the ISSUE next-action hints; add the defaulted definitionKind field to WorkflowChainDto.

migration.backwardCompat: No stored artifact changes shape, so no data is rewritten and existing ISSUE, LLD, PLAN and BUILD records stay valid. ChainReport gains one optional field only, so the VS Code and JetBrains clients that read it over IPC keep working (their parsers must ignore unknown optional fields; verify against vscode-plugin and jetbrains-plugin chain readers before build). Already-approved ISSUEs that have an orphaned standalone LLD from the old route keep that LLD; they are not migrated, and re-running design.story for such an ISSUE through the new route creates LLD-<issueHash>-s1 as a separate record. The emitted nextCall of an ISSUE approved before this change is recomputed from the stored ISSUE at advance time, so it picks up the new params with no stored state to update. Test fixtures that build a sized ISSUE gain an issueHash. The chain report no longer suggests push-tracker or sync-tracker for an ISSUE-anchored item; the tracker stages stay unchanged and DEF-only until ISSUE-5f9d4ab4c90c0b4c. The JetBrains WorkflowChainDto gains a defaulted field only, so existing callers and the Workflows page compile unchanged; DEF entries and their hints are identical.

alternativesConsidered.name: Producer-only fix
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: nextAfterIssue passes epicHash=issueHash and storyId='s1'; readers untouched.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Change only the sized branch of nextAfterIssue (src/workflow/bugfix/next-after-issue.ts) to add params.epicHash = issue.meta.issueHash and params.storyId = 's1' alongside standalone:true. The daemon start phase keeps a supplied epicHash, finalizeStandaloneLld inherits label/anchor from the ISSUE root, and design review classifies the LLD as kind issue. buildChainReport, the tracker readers and the 'run define first' advice are left exactly as they are.
pros: Smallest change; fixes the orphaned LLD identity and the design-review rejection
No change to what any reader accepts
cons: Does not fix the original reproduction: the chain report still returns zero stories and 'run-define' for an ISSUE-anchored item, now including the new LLD
Leaves the misleading 'run define first' advice and the duplicated one-implied-story rule
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Fixes the new reproduction only; the original reader defect and the misleading advice remain, so the approved ISSUE is not discharged.

alternativesConsidered.name: Producer fix plus one shared ISSUE-aware story-set read, adopted by the chain report only
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Producer retains the ISSUE anchor; one shared function states the implied-s1 rule; chain report and tracker resolver call it; design.epic keeps refusing an ISSUE.
alternativesConsidered.approach: (1) nextAfterIssue's sized branch adds epicHash=issue.meta.issueHash and storyId='s1'. (2) Add one exported helper next to readEpicDefinitionCore in src/workflow/storage.ts that reads the work item's definition head (DEF then ISSUE) and returns the declared story ids for a DEF or the single implied 's1' for an ISSUE; tracker/resolve.ts storyEvidence is changed to call it so the rule lives in one place. (3) buildChainReport reads the head through a DEF-or-ISSUE reader: an ISSUE head yields one implied story s1 with its LLD state, nextAction names the ISSUE stage (no run-define advice). (4) requireApprovedEpic stays DEF-only so design.epic and the tracker push still refuse an ISSUE, but its ArtifactMissingError is replaced, when an ISSUE root exists at that hash, by a message that names the ISSUE as the real situation.
pros: Fixes both the producer and the original reproduction while keeping the one-implied-story rule in a single place
design.epic and tracker callers keep their current acceptance, so no silent behaviour change
The misleading define advice stops for work items that can never have a Define
cons: Touches chain.ts, gates.ts, storage.ts and tracker/resolve.ts as well as the producer
Adds one shared helper that three callers must adopt correctly

alternativesConsidered.name: Make requireApprovedEpic ISSUE-aware for every caller
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: The shared gate returns a synthesized DefineArtifact for an ISSUE root.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Change requireApprovedEpic and readDefineArtifact in src/workflow/gates.ts to fall back to the ISSUE root and return a DefineArtifact synthesized from it with one story s1, so all nine callers and the chain report see an ISSUE-anchored item with no per-site change. The producer fix of a1 still applies.
pros: Single point of change for the readers; no per-caller decision
Chain report and orchestrator both recognise the item without further edits
cons: Silently changes what design.epic, tracker.push/sync/post and finalizeDefineExtend accept: an ISSUE would pass as an approved Epic and an Epic HLD could be authored for a bugfix
A synthesized DefineArtifact is a fabricated record that can be mistaken for a stored one
Contradicts the issue's own caution about changing the shared reader for everyone
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Cheapest reader fix but it is the option the issue itself warns against, and it can let an Epic HLD be authored for a bugfix.

alternativesConsidered.name: Per-caller ISSUE handling at each requireApprovedEpic site
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Each of the nine call sites decides for itself whether to tolerate an ISSUE.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Leave the shared reader alone and edit each non-test caller (readPlanUpstream, finalizeDefineExtend, finalizeDesignEpic, finalizeDesignStory, the design-story and design-epic runners, tracker context) with its own ISSUE branch, plus the chain report, plus the producer fix.
pros: Each caller can choose exactly the behaviour it wants
cons: Nine places to keep consistent; the implied-s1 rule would be re-derived at each, the exact divergence the issue warns about
Most of those sites are unreachable for an ISSUE once the LLD is standalone, so most edits would be dead code
Largest change surface and test burden
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Correct per caller but creates the third inconsistent convention and mostly dead edits.
